subject: general
question: Find the circumference (in m) of the largest circle that can be inscribed in a rectangle whose dimensions are given as 114 m and 63 m. (Take pi = (22)/(7))
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **diameter** of the **largest inscribed circle** in a rectangle is always equal to the **shorter side** of the rectangle.

Diameter (d) = 63 m

Circumference = πd = (22/7) × 63 = 22 × 9 = 198 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 198 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Length** (L) = 114 m, **Breadth** (B) = 63 m.

**Formula Used:** Diameter (d) of the largest inscribed circle = Breadth (B) of the rectangle; Circumference = π × d.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/65ecd507f0fa6d1db65a79a8ae5ec8d2cbe2d28328c948a6f02e0338159969e0.png] 

⇒ Diameter of the circle (d) = 63 m

⇒ Radius (r) = d/2 = 63/2 = 31.5 m

⇒ Circumference = 2 × π × r = π × d

⇒ Circumference = (22/7) × 63

⇒ Circumference = 22 × 9

⇒ Circumference = 198 m

**∴ The correct answer is 198 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inscribed Circle in Square

For a **square** of side 'a', the diameter of the **inscribed circle** is exactly equal to the side 'a'. Area = πa²/4.

Circumscribed Circle

The diameter of a circle **circumscribing** a rectangle is equal to the **diagonal** of the rectangle, calculated as √(L² + B²).

Circle Properties

Area of circle = πr². The **circumference** is the total boundary length, also known as the **perimeter** of the circle.</p
